items.title: Section: The Divine Ear — Twelve Kinds of Sound, and the Story of Two Rival Masters

items.zh: 謂佛菩薩以淨天耳，能於種種天聲、人聲，聖聲、非聖聲，大聲、小聲，辯聲、非辯聲，化聲、非化聲，遠聲、近聲皆悉得聞。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas, through the purified divine ear, are able to hear every kind of sound: heavenly voices and human voices, noble speech and ordinary speech, loud sounds and soft sounds, easily comprehensible speech and difficult speech, conjured sounds and genuine sounds, and sounds distant and near.

items.zh: 聞天聲者，若不作意，下從欲界，上至色究竟宮，其中受生諸有情類種種音聲皆悉能聞。若作意時，過是已上諸世界聲皆亦能聞。聞人聲者，遍於一切傍四大洲受生有情種種音聲皆悉能聞。聞聖聲者，於諸如來、聲聞、獨覺及諸菩薩，若從彼聞展轉為餘諸有情類宣說種種示現、教導、讚勵、慶慰，勸修諸善、勸捨諸惡所有音聲皆悉能聞。又於一切無染污心受持讀誦、論議決擇、無倒諫誨、為作憶念、教授、教誡，及餘所有善言善說能引義利種種音聲皆悉能聞。如是等類，名聞聖聲。聞非聖聲者，於諸有情虛妄、離間、邪綺、麁獷、生下惡趣、生上天趣、生傍人趣種種音聲皆悉能聞。聞大聲者，謂於大眾生聲、大集會聲、種種苦具所逼切聲、大號哭聲、相呼召聲、大雷吼聲、諸螺貝聲、諸鼓角等種種音聲皆悉能聞。聞小聲者，下至耳語諸微細聲皆悉能聞。
items.en: Hearing soft sounds: down to the faintest whisper or the most subtle sound, all of it can be heard.

items.zh: 聞辯聲者，於義易了種種音聲皆悉能聞。聞非辯聲者，於義難了種種音聲，謂達羅弭荼種種明呪、風、鈴、樹響、鸚鵡、鸜鵒、百舌、鸝黃、命命鳥等所出音聲、皆悉能聞。聞化聲者，謂於一切得心自在具神通者，依神通力所化音聲皆悉能聞。聞非化聲者，謂於種種異彼音聲皆悉能聞。聞遠聲者，除佛菩薩所住聚落、城邑等中所有音聲，於餘乃至無量無數世界中聲皆悉能聞。聞近聲者，聞所除聲。云何諸佛菩薩見死生智通？

items.title: Seeing Death and Rebirth — The Divine Eye's View of the Intermediate State

items.zh: 謂佛菩薩以超過人清淨天眼，見諸有情死時、生時、妙色、惡色、若劣、若勝，及於後際生已增長，諸根成熟，身諸所作善、惡、無記差別而轉。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas, through the purified divine eye surpassing that of ordinary humans, see beings at the moment of death and in the intermediate state on the way to rebirth — whether their appearance is radiant or murky, inferior or excellent — and, in what follows, see them growing after birth, their faculties maturing, their bodily, verbal, and mental actions unfolding as wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral.

items.title: Seeing the Physical World in Full Detail, and the Divine Eye and Ear's Shared Purpose

items.zh: 又現見知諸光明色、諸微細色、諸變化色、諸淨妙色，下至無間，上至色究竟宮，不由作意皆能見知。若作意時，能見上下無量無數餘世界色，亦能見傍無量無數諸世界中一切諸色，乃至能見彼彼佛土彼彼如來安坐彼彼異類大會，宣說正法，顯然無亂。
items.en: They also directly perceive luminous forms, subtle particulate forms, miraculously transformed forms, and the pure, wondrous forms of the higher heavens, from the deepest hell up to the very highest heaven, without needing to make any effort of attention. When attention is deliberately directed, they can see the forms of immeasurable, uncountable other worlds above and below, and every form throughout immeasurable, uncountable worlds in every direction, even perceiving various buddha-lands where various Tathāgatas sit amid various distinct assemblies, expounding the true teaching with perfect clarity and no confusion whatsoever.

items.zh: 又佛菩薩以淨天眼，普見十方無量無數諸有情類身之所作淨不淨業。既見彼已，隨其所應、隨其所宜，施作種種利益安樂。以淨天耳，普聞十方無量無數諸有情類語之所作淨不淨業。既聞彼已，隨其所應、隨其所宜，施作種種利益安樂。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas, through the purified divine eye, universally see the pure and impure bodily deeds of beings throughout the ten directions ... and through the purified divine ear, universally hear the pure and impure verbal deeds of beings throughout the ten directions. Having seen and heard this, they bestow whatever benefit and ease is fitting and appropriate to each.

items.zh: 是名略說諸佛菩薩天眼、天耳之所作業。云何諸佛菩薩知心差別智通？

blocks.text: Two of the superknowledges, the divine ear and the divine eye. A passage (0494b04) is untranslated.

"Through the purified divine ear, they hear every kind of sound: heavenly and human voices, noble and ordinary speech, loud and soft sounds, far and near, intelligible and unintelligible." "Down to the faintest whisper." Master Cháng Bǎi quotes an old saying that a whisper among people is heard by heaven like thunder.

The prose explains the kinds of sound: intelligible speech and unintelligible sound (foreign incantations, wind, bells, rustling trees, parrots and mynahs and other birds); sounds produced by others' supernormal power and ordinary sounds; near sounds within one's own town, and far sounds in countless other worlds.

"They see beings at the moment of death and in the intermediate state on the way to rebirth, whether their appearance is radiant or murky." Master Cháng Bǎi: "death" is the moment of dying; "birth" here is abiding in the intermediate state.
"Luminous forms, subtle particulate forms, miraculously transformed forms, the pure forms of the higher heavens, from the deepest hell to the highest heaven."
"Through the divine eye they see the pure and impure bodily deeds of beings throughout the ten directions; through the divine ear they hear their verbal deeds." Knowing these, they know how to help.

quiz.q: The divine ear hears "even the faintest whisper." What old saying does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: "a whisper among humans sounds like thunder to the gods"
quiz.why: "Hearing soft sounds: down to the faintest whisper or the most subtle sound, all of it can be heard." Master Cháng Bǎi: the ancients said, "A whisper among humans, the heavens hear as thunder."

quiz.q: The divine eye sees beings "at death and at birth." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "at birth"?
options: about to die is "death"; abiding in the intermediate state is "birth"
quiz.why: "Through the purified divine eye … see beings at the moment of death and at the moment of rebirth." Master Cháng Bǎi: when beings are about to die is "death"; abiding in the intermediate state is "birth." The English doesn't convey the intermediate state.

quiz.q: The divine eye "perceives luminous forms." How does Venerable Miào Jìng contrast human and divine bodies?
options: human bodies lack light; gods' bodies naturally shine
quiz.why: "They also directly perceive luminous forms, subtle particulate forms, miraculously transformed forms, and the pure, wondrous forms of the higher heavens." Venerable Miào Jìng: our human bodies have no light; the gods' bodies naturally shine.
